narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>I will keep twelve as it is and multiply all the numbers together.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But then we cannot see the twos and the three hiding inside twelve.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Without them, the counts of every prime go wrong, so that slip is struck.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble shows 12 kept as one block; the blocks of both rows are multiplied together; the slip's bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Break every number fully into primes before you count any copies.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>To check the second pair, multiply the two answers, and then multiply the two numbers.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Both give one thousand six hundred and twenty, so the pair of answers fits.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the words break every number into primes first and multiply back to check appear; the check lines 9 x 180 = 1620 and 45 x 36 = 1620 appear with a tick

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip keeps twelve as one block and multiplies everything. Twelve is not a prime, so its copies of two and three stay hidden and the counts go wrong.
